lessons_for_next_section: A design rule the platform claims to hold has to be stated on each interface that could break it, not merely satisfied by the shape of that interface's schema. Three of five sibling skills stating it is a convention; a reader auditing one skill against the seven rules cannot find it by comparing skills they did not open.

When a ceremony turns a convention into a validator warning, run it over the whole repository in the same session and clear what it finds. A warning that fires on skills no author owns teaches the next author to read past warnings.

Calibrate a new check against the existing tree before shipping it: the adapter-citation warning had to admit sibling entities of the same capability (two entities for one B3 row, a second swap candidate) or it would have flagged four correct rows and been silenced instead of kept.

A citation can exist, pass every verbatim check, and still point at the wrong thing. Where ids are the only trace a reader can follow, the check worth writing is whether the cited record belongs to the subject of the row, not whether it resolves.

A fix to a long-running workflow script does not reach the run already in flight: it executes the code it was launched with. Fixes to a runner that must take effect now belong in what the agents read fresh from disk each time (the brief, the skill), and the script edit is for the next launch.
